title: Is That an Order or Not
gist_ar: مشهد في الشغل بلغة دارجة: الموظفة عايزة تعرف الكلام إلزام ولا نصيحة.

before_listening.en: A workplace scene. She is trying to pin him down. Listen for whether she gets an answer.
before_listening.ar: مشهد شغل. هي بتحاول تثبّته على إجابة. ركّز هل خدت إجابة ولا لأ.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: Can I just check something. When you said I might as well finish it today — was that a 'do it today'?

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: It was a — I mean, you'd know better than me how long it takes.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: Right, but I don't know whether I'm in trouble on Monday if it's not done. That's the bit I'm after.

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: You're not in trouble. Nobody's talking about trouble. I'd have thought you'd want the leeway, honestly, most people bite my hand off for that.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: Leeway's great when I know it's leeway. When I can't tell, I do the cautious thing and stay till eight, and then you say I needn't have, and I can't work out if that's a thank you or a ticking off.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: Last time it wasn't. Last time you said it and then it came up in my review.

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: Did it? That wasn't — that's not how I meant it.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: I'm not having a go. I'm asking you to say the word 'must' when you mean must, and 'up to you' when it's up to me. That's it. That's the whole ask.

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: That feels a bit heavy-handed for what's basically a friendly working relationship.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: It feels heavy-handed to you because you're the one who gets to be vague. For me it's the difference between going home and not.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: So. Today, or up to me?

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: Up to you. Genuinely. Put it in writing if you like.

segments.speaker: Nour
segments.text: And you'll say it like that? Not 'if you get a chance'?

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: Not 'if you get a chance'. I hear it. I do it without noticing, that's the honest answer, and I'd rather you pulled me up on it.

segments.speaker: Sami
segments.text: No — thank you. I'd rather be told than have you sitting here till eight, guessing what I meant.

gist_question.q: Does she get what she asked for?
options: No — he avoids giving a straight answer right up until the very end of the conversation
Yes — he finally states plainly that it is her choice

questions.q: What does 'bite my hand off' mean?
Why does she say vagueness costs her and not him?
questions.q_ar: ليه بتقول إن الغموض بيكلّفها هي مش هو؟
options: He gets to be vague; for her it decides whether she goes home
She is paid considerably less than him and cannot afford to work the extra hours
He does not attend her reviews
Remove the comment from her review
Say 'must' when it is required and 'up to you' when it is not
